title: Bunk Johnson's playing and speech
summary: Purnell praises Bunk's distinctive style with runs on diminished chords and explains his pronunciation as coming from New Iberia.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: I think it was in the 50s, because I know I was at a station in Berkeley at the time when he passed on, and it was an awful shock to all of us because he was a great fella.
Yeah, he was a fine guy. I liked the way he played. He was so different from the rest of those other trumpet players. Musically, he used to make all these runs on the diminished chords, you know?
Uh-huh. Mm-hmm. I know also that he used to talk down by, he sang down by the riverside on one record, and he always talked about laying your weapons instead of your weapons down.
Yeah, well, Bunk comes from a new-eyed bearing that these people pronounce their words a little different from other people, you know.
I know, but it's distinctly Bunk.
